slides.title: Pudu Robotics Unveils PuduFM 1.0 and PuduAgent
slides.tldr: NEW HUMANOID AND EMBODIED AI SYSTEMS
slides.highlight: The introduction of PuduFM 1.0 and PuduAgent advances humanoid and embodied AI systems, providing relevant insights for RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

slides.title: Xingyuanzhi Robot Raises ¥1 Billion for Embodied AI Brain Technology
slides.highlight: Xingyuanzhi Robot is developing embodied AI brain technology, which aligns with RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated interaction.

slides.title: Is Telehealth Better Used to Treat Patients or Help Other Physicians Treat Patients? An Agent-Based Modeling Study of Healthcare Provision
slides.highlight: This study uses agent-based modeling to compare the effects of physician-physician versus physician-patient telehealth on clinical outcomes and system utilization, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: Telehealth is more cost-effective when providing specialist access to physicians than direct access to patients.
card.key_idea: An agent-based model simulating medical toxicology care to compare the health outcomes and costs of physician-physician versus physician-patient telehealth and poison control center consultations.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 100 simulation runs using the Mesa Python package, varying clinical complexity and toxicologist efficacy; results aligned with existing empirical toxicology data.
card.limitation: Relies on simulated data and an incomplete model that assumes perfect in-hospital diagnostic accuracy and single-problem patients.

slides.title: Modelling Opinion Dynamics at Scale with Deep MARL
slides.highlight: This research uses multi-agent reinforcement learning to model consensus and polarization in large populations, providing insights into how conformity affects collective accuracy in social networks, which is relevant to MIMIC's societal-scale simulation of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Deep MARL models opinion dynamics, suggesting modern social media scales exacerbate misinformation via evolved conformity heuristics.
card.key_idea: A GPU-accelerated consensus and truth-finding game using general-sum other-play MARL and a learned attention layer to recover agent importance from graph topology.
card.evaluation: Validated on a Bluesky network subset; compared large social media networks against small hunter-gatherer networks regarding collective accuracy and conformity.

slides.title: Toward Signing Activity Projection in Sign Language Interaction
slides.highlight: This study explores adapting Voice Activity Projection to sign language interaction using pose-derived features, contributing to HyECHO's goals regarding multimodal social perception and engagement modeling.

card.one_liner: Adapts a Voice Activity Projection framework to predict turn-taking in dyadic sign language interaction.
card.key_idea: A Transformer-based model using pose-derived hand, eye, and mouth features to predict future signing activity states over a 2-second horizon.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on Public DGS Corpus using SHIFT/HOLD and SHIFT-prediction tasks; hand cues significantly improved SHIFT/HOLD balanced accuracy and macro-F1.
card.limitation: Relies on lexical sign annotations as proxy labels, which may overstate hand cue importance and ignore sign-language-specific interactional events.

slides.title: Hierarchical Policies from Verbal and Egocentric Human Signals for Natural Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: The EDITH framework integrates first-person view, gaze, and speech to reduce user effort in human-robot interaction, supporting RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: EDITH enables robots to interpret human intent using combined verbal instructions and egocentric gaze/view signals.
card.key_idea: A hierarchical policy using a VLM high-level controller to produce subtasks (fine-grained instructions paired with keyframes) and a VLA low-level controller for execution.
card.evaluation: Tested on three HRI tasks (muffin-serving, tumbler-sorting, tool-passing); achieved 59.7% average success rate, significantly outperforming language-only baselines (<6.5%).
card.limitation: Reactivity is limited by high-level policy latency and performance degrades for users with physical attributes (e.g., height) differing from training data.

slides.title: Personalized and Robust Proactive Robot Assistance with Uncertainty-Guided LLM Reasoning
slides.tldr: ROBUST PROACTIVE ROBOT ASSISTANCE VIA LLM REASONING
slides.highlight: The GLOBE framework uses n-gram Markov models and LLM reasoning to predict human activities and object usage in noisy household environments. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: GLOBE uses n-gram Markov models and selective LLM reasoning for robust, proactive household object prediction.
card.key_idea: A lightweight framework combining n-gram Markov models for temporal patterns with an LLM that is selectively triggered via a confidence threshold to refine uncertain predictions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on HOMER+ and a new HOMER-Noise dataset against SLaTe-PRO and STOT using F1-scores; showed competitive accuracy and superior robustness to environmental noise.
card.limitation: Selective LLM invocation introduces significantly higher inference latency compared to purely sequential models due to external API calls.

slides.title: Personality Anchoring for Social Simulation: Linking Personality, Social Behavior, and Interaction Success with LLM Agents
slides.tldr: PERSONALITY ANCHORING FOR LLM SOCIAL SIMULATION
slides.highlight: This research introduces a personality anchoring pipeline to simulate how dyadic personality traits influence social behavior and goal achievement, supporting MIMIC's focus on LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: Personality anchoring using known characters reveals that dyadic Agreeableness strongly predicts shared goal achievement in LLM simulations.
card.key_idea: Agents are instantiated as well-known characters (personality anchoring) rather than via trait prompting, then interact across a validated taxonomy of human goals using structured behavior strategies.
card.evaluation: 1,010 conversations across 7 goal categories evaluated by LLM-as-a-judge; results showed high consistency (ICC=0.89) and stable personality expression.
card.limitation: Relies on LLM-as-a-judge scoring and pre-existing model knowledge of Western characters, which may introduce stereotypes and cultural bias.

slides.title: Semantically-Aware Diver Activity Recognition Framework for Effective Underwater Multi-Human-Robot Collaboration
slides.highlight: DAR-Net uses a transformer-based framework and a new dataset to recognize diver activities, supporting the development of collaborative human-robot interaction in challenging environments relevant to RwB.

card.one_liner: DAR-Net is a transformer-based framework for recognizing diver activities to improve underwater human-robot collaboration.
card.key_idea: A multi-loss training strategy combining a transformer-based classification branch with an encoder-decoder segmentation branch to align global activity recognition with local scene semantics.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new UDA dataset (2,640 images) against SOTA models; achieved 73.33% accuracy on a 30-clip test set.
card.limitation: Small dataset size and use of controlled closed-water environments may limit generalization to unpredictable open-water conditions.

slides.title: Multi-Faceted Interactivity Alignment in Full-Duplex Speech Models
slides.tldr: RL-BASED INTERACTIVITY ALIGNMENT FOR FULL-DUPLEX SPEECH
slides.highlight: This work proposes a post-training alignment method using reinforcement learning to improve pause handling, turn-taking, backchanneling, and user interruption in full-duplex models, supporting HyECHO's focus on listener modeling and engagement.

card.one_liner: A post-training RL method improving full-duplex speech model interactivity across pause, turn-taking, backchanneling, and interruption axes.
card.key_idea: Uses GRPO to optimize models on short human conversation segments with axis-specific rule-based rewards and an LLM-based semantic quality reward to prevent content degradation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated Moshi and PersonaPlex using Full-Duplex-Bench v1 (static) and v2 (real-time multi-turn with GPT-Realtime); results show consistent interactivity and fluency improvements.
card.limitation: Relies on manually engineered rule-based rewards and requires models that generate a parallel text token stream for optimization.

slides.title: Safe, Fluent and Acceptable Motion Generation and Execution for Human--Robot Interaction in Manufacturing Environments
slides.tldr: SOCIALLY-AWARE MOTION CONTROL FOR HUMAN-ROBOT INTERACTION
slides.highlight: This research explores integrating social-aware motion control and human-centered considerations into robot behavior to improve social acceptability and comfort, which is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A framework for generating socially-aware robot motions that balance physical safety, fluency, and human acceptability.
card.key_idea: An MPC-based controller using separating-plane optimization and LSTM-predicted human hand positions, parameterized by maximum velocity and interaction distance to generate four distinct social behaviors.
card.evaluation: Validated via a user study with 111 non-expert participants using NASA-TLX for workload and 10 bipolar adjective scales for social perception.
card.limitation: Interaction distance had minimal effect on most perceptual dimensions compared to the strong influence of velocity profiles.

slides.title: Fast-SDE: Efficient Single-Microphone Sound Source Distance Estimation in Reverberant Environments
slides.highlight: Fast-SDE provides a lightweight framework for sound source distance estimation using a single microphone, enhancing the naturalness of human-robot interaction on size-constrained platforms. This is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Fast-SDE is a lightweight single-microphone framework for efficient sound source distance estimation in reverberant environments.
card.key_idea: A subband-based backbone decomposes the frequency axis into non-overlapping subbands, processed by a shared encoder and a lightweight regression head (GRU or MLP) to reduce complexity.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulations (FRAM-RIR) and real-world robot experiments using MAE. Compared against SELDNet and Attention-based models across GPU, CPU, and ESP32-S3 microcontroller.
card.limitation: Estimation error increases with acoustic environment diversity and is significantly affected by the source-microphone wall-distance difference.

slides.title: Speaker Group Encoding in Self-supervised Speech Recognition Models
slides.tldr: ANALYSIS OF SPEAKER GROUP ENCODING IN S3MS
slides.highlight: This research examines how self-supervised speech recognition models encode speaker group categories such as gender, age, and dialect, which is relevant to HyECHO's focus on identity recognition and social perception.

card.one_liner: S3Ms encode speaker group information, with ASR finetuning discarding phonetic traits while retaining semantic ones.
card.key_idea: Used speaker-invariant linear probes to analyze how Wav2Vec 2.0 and WavLM encode gender, age, dialect, and ethnicity across layers during pretraining and various finetuning stages.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using Meta Fair-speech and Sonos datasets via macro F1 probing accuracy across different S3M architectures and finetuning recipes (CTC, DET, DAT).
card.limitation: Socio-economic background was not consistently detectable; ethnicity detection was poor in some models.

slides.title: Impedance MPC for Physical Human-Robot Interaction: Predictive Disturbance Rejection with Joint-Limit Safety
slides.tldr: PREDICTIVE IMPEDANCE CONTROL FOR SAFE pHRI
slides.highlight: This work introduces a two-layer Impedance MPC that achieves high trajectory accuracy and zero steady-state error during physical human-robot interaction. It is relevant to RwB for improving the safety and precision of embodied social robots during physical contact.

card.one_liner: A two-layer Impedance MPC achieving zero steady-state error and joint-limit safety for physical human-robot interaction.
card.key_idea: Analytical feedforward cancellation reduces the robot to a constant-state linear double integrator, enabling a fast 30-variable convex QP and Kalman-based disturbance estimation for offset-free tracking.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on a 7-DOF Franka FR3 in MuJoCo; outperformed classical impedance by reducing steady-state error from 44.8mm to <0.05mm under 15N force.
card.limitation: The zero-steady-state-error guarantee applies to constant or asymptotically constant disturbances; anti-windup behavior under persistent saturation requires further formal proof.
